answer: Sybil resistance arises when each challenge commits to a future threshold-BLS beacon pulse whose value is unknowable at issuance. The pulse derives task parameters, nonce domains, and verification salts—such as prism, quartz, and knoll—only after commitment, so automated identities cannot precompute valid answers, reuse cached work, or farm solutions offline. Unpredictable reveal timing and publicly verifiable signatures further prevent coalition bias.
